title: The adult game crackdown is "ridiculous for our art form", say Hellraiser devs, but they think they'll survive thanks to that Clive Barker association
description: Last year, Australian anti-porn group Collective Shout pressured payment processors, such as Mastercard, Paypal, Visa, and Paysafe Limited to withdraw their services from Steam and Itch.io if the stores didn't remove adult games from their shelves. The campaign was successful and many games were impacted. The campaign's had a chilling effect, leaving developers making games including any sexual content in a kind of limbo as to whether digital storefronts will host their work. Some are ushered through without issue, while others are banned with little recourse. Just last week, we saw how Valve blocked Molleindustria's Future? No Thanks! due to its scenes of minor nudity. Then, only after public lobbying, did they manage to get Valve to reconsider and rescind their ban. So, after playing a half hour demo of Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival, a demo set almost entirely inside a fetish club, and one featuring male nudity, female nudity, and some pretty sexually explicit content, I asked the developers if they were worried about a Steam ban or if it had led to any changes to the game. title: Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices
description: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement ( via IGN ) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible for a payment. The lawsuit, originally filed back in 2024, alleged that Sony established a monopoly over PlayStation Store prices by making publishers "cede control over the final price to Sony" and that Sony "eliminated the last vestiges of price competition when it stopped allowing outside retailers to sell digital download codes that could be redeemed on the PlayStation Store." Sony is not agreeing to wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and will be avoiding a civil trial if the terms are agreed upon by the court. Once that happens, the claims against Sony will be dismissed "with prejudice," meaning another lawsuit on the subject cannot be filed. You are potentially eligible for a payout if you purchased one of the affected games via the PlayStation Store between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. Dozens of games are listed in the official court documents, including Nier: Automata, Resident Evil 4, The Last of Us Remastered, and Vita games like Uncharted: Golden Abyss and Killzone: Mercenary.

title: GTA 6’s Extended Look Trailer Seemingly Paid Off For Netflix With Massive Viewership
description: Netflix has confirmed that GTA 6's recent "extended look" trailer was the streamer's most-viewed title overall last week, drawing 31.1 million views. The trailer was labeled an "English-language film" by Netflix, and it was No. 1 by that designation in 87 of 93 regions globally that Netflix's tracks ( via Variety ). The GTA 6 trailer was well ahead of the No. 2 title last week, which was the movie The Whisper Man, which had 23.2 million viewers. Netflix's view counts cover views for each title from Monday to Sunday of the previous week. A "view" is defined by Netflix as the total hours viewed divided by the total runtime. Netflix publishes this data each Tuesday. The extended look trailer was published first on Netflix before being released on Rockstar's own YouTube channel and elsewhere six hours later. Rockstar's own video has 17 million views, but YouTube counts views differently, and that represents just one channel, as numerous other sites and sources hosted it, including here at GameSpot. Netflix called its partnership with Rockstar Games for the trailer a "first-of-its-kind" offering for the popular streaming platform. Netflix's stock price has crashed since its bailed out of its deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery, and the company has undertaken numerous efforts to increase engagement and total watching time on the platform. Beyond this partnership for the GTA 6 trailer, Netflix has expanded into video podcasts. The New York Times recently reported that Netflix is in discussions to add Fox One and Peacock to the platform, while it's also been reported that Netflix could add free ad-supported TV content. As for GTA 6, the game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: Fortnitemares Is A Spooky Dream Come True At Universal’s Horror Nights
description: While Halloween is drawing nearer, the clock is ticking before Epic Games reveals this year's Fortnitemares event, which will carry Fortnite through spooky season with haunting new skins, bosses, weapons, and points of interest on the map. Until that drops, though, there is another way to get your Fortnitemares fix if you happen to be visiting Universal Studios in Orlando or Hollywood. This year's Halloween Horror Nights (HHN) event has continued the recent trend of gaming properties having a major presence. The past few years have seen The Last of Us, Fallout, and Five Nights at Freddy's brought to life, thanks in no small part to the popularity of the live-action adaptations of each. This year, Fortnite takes center stage with Fortnitemares scare zones based on the annual celebration of all things horror taking place on both coasts, with each park getting a unique take on the event. To adapt Fortnitemares, creative teams at both Universal parks worked with Epic Games to craft an experience that feels genuine to the experience of traversing a Fortnite island. Speaking to GameSpot, Universal Studios Orlando creative development show director Ramón Paradoa set the stage. Guests are dropped into the middle of Freaky Fields, a Fortnitemares location from the past two years (Chapter 5, Season 4 and Chapter 6, Season 4) during a battle royale round. "You've got pumpkins. You've got scarecrows. You've got cornfields. You've got barns. You've got a bunch of creepy jack-o'-lanterns with glowing faces. A lot of things that you expect and feel like Halloween comfort food," he explained. "But how do we take it further?" Fortnitemares at Halloween Horror Nights That's the process Paradoa refers to as "HHNifying" the property, going beyond adapting the aesthetics and finding a way to make it immersive. In Orlando, that starts as you enter the zone and are faced with a version of a character-select screen, with Skull Trooper Jonesy as the chosen skin. Your mission is to survive…

title: Releasing Cyberpunk 2077 In Its Poor State “Was For Sure Wrong,” CD Projekt Admits
description: CD Projekt Red's RPG Cyberpunk 2077 infamously launched in December 2020 in such a poor technical state that Sony took the rare move to remove it from the PlayStation Store. Thousands of people refunded the game. CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski has now reflected on this, saying it "was for sure wrong" to launch the game in that state, but he pushed back against the theory that the studio did so to appease investors who wanted to see financial returns. Speaking to The Game Business, Nowakowski said COVID "was a factor" in the game's rough state at launch, because "the team was getting exhausted in a different way." He admitted there were "people outside telling us we should launch," and fans lobbied for this as well. The developers themselves also "wanted to push it out the door" because the ongoing development was "really tiring." Looking back on it, now with the benefit of hindsight, Nowakowski said, "The decision to launch was for sure wrong, period. There is no denying it." That being said, Nowakowski said, "There were no magical investors telling us, 'You have to get this out.'" Instead, he said, "It was much more complicated and psychological." A scene from Cyberpunk 2077. CD Projekt's fiscal years follow the calendar and end on December 31. Cyberpunk 2077 was released on December 10 in 2020, and this timing led people to wonder if the developer put the game out then instead of delaying to 2021 to meet the fiscal deadline. There is, after all, precedent for game developers pushing games out the door in a rough state to hit certain fiscal deadlines. Cyberpunk 2077 might have released in a rough technical state, but it was a smashing success at launch commercially. The game sold nearly 14 million copies right out of the gate, which made it one of the most successful RPG releases in the history of video games. Given that success, CD Projekt Red executives got multimillion-dollar bonus payouts, while developers also took home big bonus payouts related to…

The Witcher 4 will set the standard for what a Witcher game in Unreal Engine looks like, and it appears that The Witcher 1’s remake ( announced in 2022 ) got caught up in that technology shift. description: The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 open beta was supposed to end today, September 1, at 10 AM PT / 1 PM ET, but Activision is extending it. The beta is now set to wrap up at 10 PM PT / 1 AM ET (September 2), meaning it's been extended by a full 12 hours. Not only that, but Activision is offering double progression XP and double weapon XP now until the beta closes down. This is great news for anyone grinding through the levels to claim the MW4 open beta's various rewards. Players who make it all the way to the level cap of 30 get a special weapon blueprint, and now there are 12 more hours to grind for it, or likely less if you're at work, school, eating, sleeping, gardening, etc. After the beta wraps up, the next time people will be able to play MW4 multiplayer is when the game launches on October 23. The game's single-player campaign, meanwhile, unlocks a week before that for people who preorder. MW4 is in development for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC. The game is coming to a Nintendo platform for the first time since 2013's Call of Duty: Ghosts. Additionally, MW4 is skipping last-gen consoles for the first time since Ghosts. Metroidvania Still Feels Like A Niche Genre That Deserves Better
description: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week. Within the vast and overcrowded Steam store, there are over 3,100 titles with the “metroidvania” tag. Last year, Hollow Knight: Silksong accomplished a rare feat for an indie game, crashing storefronts upon its launch. And later this year, one of the genre’s namesakes is making a comeback in the form of the 2D action game Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse. And yet, 40 years after the release of the original Metroid and Castlevania games, the genre influenced by those two beloved franchises still feels relatively obscure. The metroidvania or “search-action” genre has long felt like a middle child among the wider family of (arguably arbitrary) game classifications. For whatever reason, much of the gaming industry--particularly at the AAA level--seem hesitant to try their hands with entries to the metroidvania canon the same way they do with other budding genres. The "metroidvania" tag on Steam is packed Pick any time period in the history of games and you’ll recall moments when certain types of games were all the rage. From the cartoon-mascot platformers that plagued consoles in response to Mario and Sonic, to every publisher pushing out a “Halo killer,” and PUBG triggering an onslaught of battle royales, so many genres had their moment. The list goes on, particularly for subgenres spawning from specific games--your souls-likes, roguelikes, and such. Metroid and Castlevania each underwent early peaks and long periods of radio silence. After Super Metroid--which set the template for metroidvanias that came after--a long drought followed, with Fusion and the Prime games reviving the brand, and stinkers like Other M beginning another dark era until MercurySteam’s Samus Returns and Dread. title: Metroidvania Games Were The Original Open-World Games
description: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week. When many people pick up a controller to play a game, they're looking for one thing above all others: escapism. A break from the real world. There's no better way to do that than to immerse yourself in another world. Getting lost in a completely fictional world is true escapism. These days, open-world games like Cyberpunk 2077, Red Dead Redemption 2, and the most recent Legend of Zelda games do a lot of the work here, giving us maps full of icons to wade through. But the original escapist games came in the form of search-action games, colloquially known as metroidvania games by their fans. The term metroidvania has been around since the early 2000s, and mashes together the names of two games that established the tropes of the genre early on, Metroid and Castlevania. A classic metroidvania game drops you at the entrance to an environment that feels massive (especially in the opening hours) and gives you a pretty straightforward quest like "defeat Dracula"--and then throws countless roadblocks in your path on the way to that goal (locked doors, impassable areas, area bosses), forcing you to crisscross a growing map of different, visually distinct areas, often with their own enemies and thematically appropriate challenges. Animal Well, a densely packed metroidvania Those roadblocks are key to making the exploration feel like it matters. You can't go anywhere you like at the beginning; you'll need to unlock ways to open doors and new movement options to let you bypass hazards. When you eventually get through that barrier and into a new biome, that sense of wonder at seeing a new place can set in. Those roadblocks look a little different in open-world games; some games eschew these roadblocks entirely in favor of freedom, while…
